# Temple Scroll Column 55 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 55 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**55:1** When you lend to your neighbor a loan of any thing, you shall not go into his house to take his pledge.

**55:2** In the outside you shall stand, and the man to whom you are lending shall bring out the pledge to you, to the outside.

**55:3** And if the man is poor, you shall not lie down in his pledge.

**55:4** Returning, you shall return to him the pledge when the sun goes down, and he shall lie down in his garment and bless you; and to you it shall be righteousness before the LORD your God.

**55:5** You shall not oppress a hired-one who is poor and needy, from your brothers or from the sojourner who is in your land, in your gates.

**55:6** In his day you shall give his wage, and the sun shall not go down upon it, for he is poor and to it he lifts his soul; so that he does not cry out against you to the LORD, and it be in you a sin.

**55:7** Fathers shall not be put to death on account of sons, and sons shall not be put to death on account of fathers; each man in his own sin shall be put to death.

**55:8** You shall not pervert the judgment of a sojourner or an orphan, and you shall not take-as-a-pledge the garment of a widow.

**55:9** And you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from there; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.

**55:10** When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not return to take it; it shall be for the sojourner, for the orphan, and for the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in every work of your hands.

**55:11** When you beat your olive-tree, you shall not go over it again after you; it shall be for the sojourner, for the orphan, and for the widow.

**55:12** When you gather your vineyard, you shall not glean it after you; it shall be for the sojourner, for the orphan, and for the widow.

**55:13** And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.

**55:14** When there is a dispute between men and they draw near to the judgment, and they judge them, and they declare-righteous the righteous-one and declare-guilty the guilty-one —

**55:15** and it shall be, if the guilty-one is a son of striking, then the judge shall make him lie down and strike him before him according to his guilt, by number.

**55:16** Forty strokes he may strike him; he shall not add, lest he add to strike him beyond these with many strokes, and your brother be degraded in your eyes.

---

*EMET notes: Column 55 reworks Deuteronomy 24:10-25:3. "Hired-one" for sakhir preserves the Hebrew participle. "Son of striking" — literally "deserving of blows." The triple gleaning law (field, olive, vineyard) is preserved with its motivation clause linking to the Egypt memory. "Declare-righteous/declare-guilty" preserves the Hebrew hiphil causative forms.*
